source_code_review_20260925.provenance: User pasted the verified Solidity source. PRIMARY SOURCE - second asset in this file confirmed from primary rather than search summary.
source_code_review_20260925.template: BokkyPooBah / Bok Consulting 'Moritz Neto' ERC20 template, 2017 vintage. Widely copy-pasted boilerplate, not bespoke code.
source_code_review_20260925.compiler: ^0.4.24 (Etherscan reports v0.4.24+commit.e67f0147) - consistent with the Feb 2020 creation date, unlike 0x46493b80 whose 0.8.14 compiler disproved its claimed 2020 date.
source_code_review_20260925.supply_math: _totalSupply = 2100000000000000 with decimals = 8 -> exactly 21,000,000 whole tokens. Confirms the Bitcoin-cap mirror.
source_code_review_20260925.genesis_allocation: 100% of supply hardcoded to 0xb943B74B93485B9Cb47E614C54e946D7c16ad2c8 in the constructor. Total concentration at genesis in a single wallet.
source_code_review_20260925.owner_vs_recipient: owner = msg.sender (deployer, set in Owned constructor); supply recipient is a separate hardcoded literal. They may or may not be the same party.
absent_by_design: no mint function - supply is fixed and cannot be inflated
no proxy or upgrade path - logic is immutable
no bridge, no cross-chain messaging, no lock/mint hooks
source_code_review_20260925.assessment: Mechanically CLEAN. None of the honeypot or rug primitives are present. Its risk is not the code - it is zero liquidity and 100% genesis concentration.
minor_defects: transfer() has no zero-address check - tokens can be burned to 0x0 by mistake
classic ERC20 approve() race condition (acknowledged in the source comments)

known_assets.cross_chain_note: Same address 0xf938c9a2... is indexed on BOTH Etherscan and BscScan, and served by poocoin.app (BSC-only) and Bitget web3 /swap/bnb/. This is address reuse, NOT a bridged asset: an EVM CREATE address is keccak256(rlp(deployer, nonce))[12:], so the same deployer key at the same nonce yields the same address on every EVM chain. The contract has NO bridge or cross-chain logic, so the ETH and BSC deployments are disjoint ledgers with independent prices. NOT a new listing.

project_description.text: FRNK aims to complete the blockchain-based cryptocurrency ecosystem by actual application and diffusion as a means of exchanging with the real economy, which is the next step of the decentralized distributed ledger hypothesis proposed in Bitcoin, and to complete the verification of the hypothesis.
project_description.source: Aggregator OVERVIEW panel (Bitget/CoinMarketCap-style), user-supplied screenshot. Project-submitted copy, so it is the project's own words.
project_description.content_analysis: No mechanism, sector, product, partner or user named. Reduces to 'FRNK will be used in the real economy'. Every clause is aspiration or a restatement of Bitcoin's existing premise.
project_description.bitcoin_framing_error: Bitcoin did not propose a 'hypothesis' awaiting verification - it has run continuously since January 2009. Framing it as unverified, with FRNK to 'complete the verification', is grandiose framing around no claim.
project_description.NO_SIMPSONS_REFERENCE: CRITICAL: the description never mentions The Simpsons, Professor Frink, or memes. It reads as an earnest payments/social-coin pitch.

bok_consulting_attribution.header_line: (c) by Moritz Neto with BokkyPooBah / Bok Consulting Pty Ltd Au 2017. The MIT Licence.
bok_consulting_attribution.who: BokkyPooBah = Bok Khoo, director of Bok Consulting Pty Ltd (Australia). Real and well-regarded: actuary and quantitative developer, ~28 years industry experience, working on Ethereum since 2015, known smart-contract auditor, author of widely used libraries (DateTime, RedBlackTree) and of the TokenTrader / Token Teleportation contracts.
bok_consulting_attribution.what_it_means: NOTHING about FRNK. It is the MIT copyright notice of the ERC20 TEMPLATE the deployer copied. The MIT licence REQUIRES retaining the notice, so its presence is licence compliance - not authorship, endorsement, involvement, review or audit of FRNK.
bok_consulting_attribution.scale_of_reuse: GitHub code search for the exact phrase 'with BokkyPooBah / Bok Consulting Pty Ltd Au' in Solidity returns 25,536 files (verified 2026-09-25 via GitHub API). Top hit is bitfwdcommunity/ICO-tutorial - the template's origin is teaching material for 'how to issue your own token'.
bok_consulting_attribution.staleness_evidence: The header says 2017; FRNK was deployed February 2020. Like the '// Deployed to :' line (which names the supply recipient, not the contract), it is unedited template text. Two independent stale artifacts in the same header show the deployer did not modify the boilerplate.
bok_consulting_attribution.misreading_risk: Because Bok Consulting is a genuine auditing firm, this line is easily mistaken for a credibility signal or an audit. There is no audit of FRNK, and no relationship between Bok Consulting and this token.

known_assets.name: Frinkcoin (FRNK) - BSC deployment at the SAME address
known_assets.provenance: User pasted the deployed runtime bytecode. PRIMARY SOURCE - third asset in this file confirmed from primary rather than search summary.
known_assets.relationship_to_eth_frnk: SAME ADDRESS, DIFFERENT CONTRACT. Proven at the bytecode level, not inferred.

proof_of_difference.decimals: BSC returns 18 (opcode sequence 6000 6012 90 50 90 -> PUSH1 0x12). Ethereum FRNK returns 8. A different decimals value alone makes them different tokens.
proof_of_difference.compiler: BSC CBOR metadata: solc 0.8.1. Ethereum: solc 0.4.24. Solidity 0.8.1 was released January 2021, so the BSC contract was deployed NO EARLIER than Jan 2021 - at least ~11 months after the Ethereum FRNK (created Feb 2020, verified 2020-04-12). Same compiler-version dating technique that debunked the 0x46493b80 'Feb 2020' claim.
proof_of_difference.codebase: BSC is stock OpenZeppelin ERC20 v4.x - identified by its revert strings ('ERC20: transfer to the zero address' etc.) and OZ storage layout (balances slot 0, allowances 1, totalSupply 2, name 3, symbol 4). Ethereum is the BokkyPooBah/'Moritz Neto' 2017 template. Unrelated code lineages.
proof_of_difference.dispatcher_size: Exactly 11 external functions - the ERC20 interface and nothing else.

known_assets.ownership: NO owner at all. No Ownable, no admin functions, no privileged role in the runtime bytecode. Fully ownerless - nobody can mint, pause, blacklist or sweep. Structurally cleaner than the Ethereum version, which at least retains an owner.
known_assets.payable: Non-payable: CALLVALUE/ISZERO guard at the entry point rejects BNB on every function. No fallback.
known_assets.not_readable_from_runtime: Total supply, name and symbol are set in the CONSTRUCTOR, which is not part of runtime bytecode. Cannot confirm the BSC supply is 21,000,000 from this paste alone.
known_assets.price_linkage: NONE. No bridge, no mint, no cross-chain messaging on either side. The two deployments are disjoint ledgers. Arbitrage is impossible, so ETH and BSC prices cannot converge.
known_assets.notes: NOT a new listing. Address reuse is deterministic (CREATE address = keccak256(rlp(deployer, nonce))[12:]), so the same deployer key at the same nonce yields the same address on every EVM chain.
known_assets.supply: 21,000,000,000 (21 BILLION) - 1,000x the Ethereum FRNK supply of 21,000,000. The BSC version ABANDONS the Bitcoin-cap mirror.
known_assets.supply_confidence: SINGLE SOURCE (one search summary quoting BscScan). Not independently corroborated; explorers are egress-blocked. The same summary reported the Ethereum figures correctly (21,000,000 / 29 holders), which is mild support that it is distinguishing the two rather than conflating them.

concentration_20260925.significance: This is the SAME address hardcoded in the Ethereum constructor to receive 100% of supply. One wallet is the treasury on BOTH chains.

known_assets.operator_inference: The shared treasury wallet plus the shared contract address together establish the same operator behind both deployments. A CREATE address is keccak256(rlp(deployer, nonce))[12:], so reproducing 0xf938c9a2... on BSC required the same deployer EOA at the same nonce - i.e. control of that key. The address reuse is deliberate, not coincidental.
known_assets.risk_reassessment: Code is clean (ownerless, no mint/burn/pause) but that does NOT make the token safe. Immutability prevents INFLATION; it does nothing about a 61% holder SELLING. With BSC liquidity reported as N/A and price $0.00, the overhang is either unsellable (no pool) or catastrophic (tiny pool). Risk has moved from the code to the cap table.

source_availability.explorer_verified: LIKELY NOT. The user retrieved runtime BYTECODE rather than Solidity, which is what BscScan serves when a contract is unverified. Not yet confirmed - check whether BscScan shows a 'Contract Source Code Verified' banner or only a Bytecode tab.
source_availability.compiler_version_caveat: solc 0.8.1 here was decoded from the CBOR metadata trailer INSIDE the bytecode, NOT read off a verified source page. Do not treat a known compiler version as proof of verification for this contract.
source_availability.cid_derivation: CBOR trailer key 'ipfs' -> multihash 0x1220 + sha2-256 digest 370e2831adc752824a59d77ed9fa264ef8e5b4682574536d38568d3ed8c500fe -> base58 -> CIDv0. If the deployer pinned it, this resolves to the full solc metadata JSON including original sources. ipfs.io is EGRESS_BLOCKED here, so unretrieved.
source_availability.effective_transparency: Even unverified, the contract is NOT opaque: revert strings and storage layout identify it as stock OpenZeppelin ERC20 v4.x, and the 11-selector dispatcher was fully enumerated. Absence of mint/burn/pause/owner was established from bytecode directly, without needing source.

CRITICAL FALSE POSITIVE: exchange 'price pages' (coinbase.com/price/..., bitget.com/price/..., binance.com/price/...). These exist for thousands of assets the exchange does NOT list for trading and are auto-generated. A price page is NEVER evidence of a listing. Only a dated announcement from the exchange's own newsroom/announcements feed counts.

Inflated market-cap figures on aggregator pages (e.g. Bitget showing FRNK at $0.006804 / $142.89M mcap) that contradict $0 24h volume elsewhere. Market cap = price x supply and is meaningless without liquidity; a dead token can show a large mcap. Not a listing signal.

CRITICAL FALSE POSITIVE: DEX aggregators, routers, wallets and trading bots (Jupiter, Phantom, Maestro Bot, Soul Sniper, MEXC DEX+, 1inch etc.) 'supporting' a token. These surface ANY token with an on-chain pool automatically - they are not listings and involve no exchange decision. 'MEXC DEX+' in particular is MEXC's on-chain aggregator front-end and is NOT a MEXC centralized-exchange listing.

Same contract address appearing on a second chain's explorer (e.g. FRNK 0xf938c9a2... on both Etherscan and BscScan). EVM addresses are deterministic from deployer+nonce, so cross-chain address reuse is trivial and means nothing. Not a bridge, not a listing, and prices on the two chains are unlinked.

frink_language_founder_watch.subject: Alan Eliasen - designer and implementer of the Frink programming language (frinklang.org), first released Dec 2001. Also authored several faster BigInteger algorithms in Java 8.
frink_language_founder_watch.naming_link: Eliasen named the LANGUAGE after Professor Frink from The Simpsons - the same character the episode's fictional coin is named for. So the language and the memecoins share a source, not a lineage.
frink_language_founder_watch.finding_20260911: NO EVIDENCE that Alan Eliasen has launched, endorsed, or been involved with any cryptocurrency. Multiple searches across his name, the language, and crypto/blockchain terms returned only his programming-language work. No token names him as founder.
frink_language_founder_watch.no_disclaimer_found: Could not locate any statement on frinklang.org either claiming or disclaiming affiliation with any FRINK token.
frink_language_founder_watch.caution: Absence of evidence from web search is not proof. But the pattern here is the opposite of a founder launch: tokens borrowing a name, with no named team.

deep_search_20260916.whitepaper: NONE FOUND. No paper authored by Eliasen on arXiv or SSRN relating to blockchain, cryptocurrency or distributed ledgers. Searches return only unrelated authors' blockchain papers.
deep_search_20260916.team: NO TEAM FOUND. Frink is consistently attributed to Alan Eliasen alone across Wikipedia, Rosetta Code, the Amazon Appstore listing and frinklang.org, since Dec 2001. It appears to be a solo project, so there is no 'team' to have crypto involvement.
deep_search_20260916.wikipedia_blockchain_list: He does NOT appear on Wikipedia's 'List of people in blockchain technology'.
deep_search_20260916.CRITICAL_FALSE_POSITIVE: frinklang.org hosts files named cryptoProviders.frink and cryptoAES256.frink. These are CRYPTOGRAPHY samples - they enumerate Java Cryptography Architecture providers and demonstrate AES-256 encryption/decryption. They have NOTHING to do with cryptocurrency. This is the single most likely source of a false 'Frink language does crypto' association and must not be reported as crypto involvement.
deep_search_20260916.known_channels: X/Twitter account @Frinklang exists (language account). OEIS wiki profile exists. No crypto content found on either.
deep_search_20260916.conclusion: No evidence of any cryptocurrency work, whitepaper, token, or blockchain involvement by Alan Eliasen, and no team exists around the language.

token_affiliation_deepdive_20260916.question: Does any token claim association with the Frink PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE (frinklang.org)?
token_affiliation_deepdive_20260916.answer: NO. No token found claims technical, official or endorsed affiliation with the language. Multiple independent sources explicitly state the tokens and the language are unrelated and share the name only via the Simpsons character.
token_affiliation_deepdive_20260916.only_adjacency_found: The FRINK Token (Polygon, frinktoken.net) has a GitHub repository tagged under the 'frink' TOPIC - the same topic tag used by Frink-language repos. This places the token's repo alongside language repos when browsing github.com/topics/frink. This is ADJACENCY BY TAG, not a claim of affiliation, but it is the one place where a browser could form a false impression.
token_affiliation_deepdive_20260916.marketing_claim_to_flag: The project states '100% liquidity locked and no rug pull risk until November 25, 2026'. 'No rug pull risk' is OVERSTATED. A liquidity lock prevents LP withdrawal only; it does not prevent the team dumping held tokens, does not rule out mint or blacklist functions in an unaudited contract, and expires on that date. Treat the phrase as marketing, not a security guarantee.
token_affiliation_deepdive_20260916.conclusion: No token is associated with the Frink programming language. The 17 FRINK-named assets and the language independently take their name from Professor Frink.
